newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares steady, Olivetti sees exodus.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares steady, Olivetti sees exodus.

text.p: Italian shares ended with mild gains on Tuesday but the crisis-struck Olivetti group was once more at the centre of selling attention, ending close to its latest record low as investors dumped the stock.

Traders said institutional investors, particularly London-based ones, seized the chance of a slight bounce to make a mass exit from the stock and volumes were substantial with 88 million Olivetti shares traded.

"Institutional investors have reached their pain threshold. The selling continued on 88 million shares traded and people were doing it ahead of any announcement by stock market regulator Consob. They're no longer waiting for any news to get out," one broker here said.
Olivetti hit a fresh record low of 555 lire, 8.0 percent down on the day after a near 20 percent plummet on Monday and a near 30 percent decline from its opening price last Monday.
It closed 5.88 percent down on the day at 567.8 lire.
"It may have hit the bottom for now so long as no more news comes out," another broker said.
Stock market watchdog Consob said it expected Olivetti to furnish the replies to seven questions on the state of its accounts, after it gave the group one day to respond on Monday.
Olivetti said it was working to meet the deadline.
Dairy products company Parmalat fell 2.47 percent to 1936 lire amid a botulism scare linked to mascarpone cheese.

Parmalat said none of its products were linked to "presumed bacterial poisoning." But brokers said the group needed to make strong sign that it was taking some action, in order to counteract growing panic over the scare.
Carmaker Fiat had a shaky day, falling 2.04 percent to 4461 after August car registrations showed a 7.50 percent decline on August 1995.
Banking stocks had a slight bounce after a decline in recent days. The blue-chip Mib30 index ended 0.73 percent up at 14121 while the all-share Mibtel index closed 0.57 percent higher at 9485.
